newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open bourse trade lower before data.
newsitem.headline: German shares open bourse trade lower before data.

text.p: German shares opened bourse trade in Frankfurt on Tuesday sharply lower, before recovering lost ground a little early on, with the markets anxiously awaiting U.S. data later in the day.
With the U.S. markets closed on Monday for the Labor Day holiday and an absence of corporate data at home, German markets were looking for new impetus to boost trade.
In early bourse trade the DAX index of German shares was down 9.35 points, or 0.37 percent, at 2,523.53 points, and lower German debt was not helping the market's mood.
Data expected included the U.S. leading indicator index for July at 1230 GMT, National Association of Purchasing Managers index at 1400 GMT and August car sales.
The news that the U.S. had launched missile attacks on Iraqi air defence targets did not have much impact, but it did lift the dollar by half a pfennig against the mark.
"It is extremely quiet here and the market is not yet focusing on the U.S./Iran conflict," said one Frankfurt dealer.
News of the higher dollar did little to boost chemical stocks, which is normally the expected reaction to a stronger U.S. currency.
BASF AG was down 11 pfennigs at 43.67 marks, while Hoechst AG was down 16 pfennigs at 51.32 marks and Bayer AG was down 10 pfennigs at 52.35 marks.
Deutsche Bank was lower on newspaper reports that funds had been suspended at its Deutsche Morgan Grenfell unit.
Deutsche was down 42 pfennigs at 72.45 marks early on.
